title: Adolph Alexander on alto and saxophone
summary: Discussion of the young Adolph Alexander versus his father, Tats's father, and saxophone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: We used Adolph Alexander on the Alto. Was that the young Adolph Alexander or his father? No, no. The young Alexander played with me once, you know, in my history. Yes. He played, coming playing saxophone, Tornet, and playing saxophone.

He played with me. He played with me. He played with me. I think he was a little older than me. I think he was a little older than me. Him and Joe Piaier, I believe, was an old Alto player. He played wrestling many times. We used Adolph Alexander on the Alto.
Is that the young Adolph Alexander or his father? No, no.

The young Alexander played with me once, you know, in my history. Yes. He played, coming playing saxophone, Tornet, and I was the one who got in to play saxophone. He started playing saxophone after he was with me. He didn't want to get on it. He didn't like it. The last step on behind him, he made good at it. He played saxophone. Arthur Durbany, he used to play with me.
The man in the band though, the Adolph Alexander, is that Tatt's father? That's right.
That's Tatt's father. He was a very good old timeist, isn't he? He was a kid.
I never knew him, I heard of him though.
